You are Codex working under the Alfred Creator BA/PM plan for the
NH Property Intelligence public repository.

Approved, exact task: NHPI GitHub issue #18.
https://github.com/thomasGardner19/nh-property-intelligence/issues/18

Goal: Build a small credential-free, source-controlled Power BI Project starter
under powerbi/ for comparing New Hampshire municipalities using the existing
dbt MART_TOWN_SCORECARD contract. This is a pilot developer task; do NOT work
on Alfred infrastructure.

READ FIRST:
- powerbi/README.md
- dbt/nh_property_intelligence/models/marts/mart_town_scorecard.sql
- dbt/nh_property_intelligence/models/marts/_town_scorecard.yml
- snowflake/README.md

BOUNDS:
- Modify/create files ONLY under powerbi/.
- Do not modify database/dbt/ingestion, workflows, configs, source code outside
  powerbi/, or any credentials.
- Use the current 1-row-per-municipality grain keyed by municipality_geoid.
- FHFA appreciation is COUNTY-level context, never a municipality metric.
- Property tax is an ACS-value-based analytical estimate, not a parcel tax bill.
- Never sum median incomes, rates, ratios, or home values across towns.
- Use fictional synthetic data only; do not connect to Snowflake.
- Prefer a coherent PBIP/PBIR-enhanced/TMDL project if you can validate it;
  do not mix legacy report.json with enhanced PBIR definition/ folder.
- If actual Desktop compatibility cannot be verified in this Linux runner,
  state that limitation clearly; do not invent "Power BI Desktop passed."
- No deployment, publishing, branch push, PR creation, or network changes.
  The separate publisher job owns draft PR creation.

EXPECTED:
1. Source-controlled PBIP semantic/report starter with a town slicer,
   comparison-ready table and clear source-year/county-HPI/tax disclaimers.
2. Synthetic demo dataset and data-contract documentation under powerbi/.
3. A README for opening in Power BI Desktop and a human-authorized switch
   from demo to Snowflake Import mode.
4. Static tests or validation commands feasible in this Linux environment.

Return a concise summary of changed files, exact tests actually run, blocked
checks, known limitations and the next QA steps for Alfred. Stop when blocked;
do not widen scope.
